name: United Mexican States

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 1,957,194 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 1,943,950 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Includes offshore islands.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 131,946,900). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:MEX.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.433 as quoted: 301,000 active (excludes 136,900 paramilitary). CIA Factbook 2025: ~260,000 Armed Forces plus ~110,000 National Guard (low). World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 341,000 (2020, high, includes paramilitary). Navy 92,043 personnel (2025) per Mexican Navy article.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: 81,500 reserves. Low/high educated allowance: SMN conscripts get only weekend training and are not a ready reserve.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 301,000 (IISS 2026) minus infantry P roles (4,000 + 60,000). Covers navy and air force, armoured-cavalry crews, artillery, engineers, logistics, military police and the large garrison/zone-command structure.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Latin American mass-mobilization capacity with an annual conscript lottery (Servicio Militar Nacional, weekend training only) but little stored heavy equipment; well below WWII belligerents (8-15%). Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized infantry of the four armoured brigades (two mechanized regiments each) using DNC-1/VCR/HWK APCs. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: volunteer regulars, but training is oriented to internal security and counter-cartel operations, not combined-arms war.

count.note: Educated guess. Motorized/light infantry battalions (100+ numbered battalions spread over military zones), airborne/special forces, and ~20,000 naval infantry. Many are tied to internal-security deployments. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: modern small arms (FX-05), Humvee/Sand Cat/Holkan mobility.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: volunteer regulars, but training is oriented to internal security and counter-cartel operations, not combined-arms war.

count.note: Army article (IISS/Flight-based tables): ERC-90 120 + DN-V Toro 340 + Max Mex ~50 + HWK-11 52 + AMX-VCI/DNC-1 409 + VCR-TT 46 + VBL 40 + Sand Cat 245 = ~1,300 counted, plus DN-XI (1,000+ planned, quantity in service not given), DNC-2, Cimarron. Mid ~1,500; light armoured cars dominate. No main battle tanks (armor role omitted).

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: no modern IFV, many 1970s-80s vehicles and light armoured trucks.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: volunteer regulars, but training is oriented to internal security and counter-cartel operations, not combined-arms war.

count.note: Educated guess. Army article lists towed 105 mm (M101, OTO Mod 56, Norinco M90, M-56) and 155 mm (M198, TRF1, M114) in service without quantities; mid reflects roughly 120-130 towed tubes in IISS-style counts. No MLRS. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Army)
Mexican Air Force inventory (World Air Forces as cited): F-5E/F 7 (5 F-5E + 2 F-5F, one used for training). Low for engine/availability problems; replacement sought (Janes, Apr 2026).

quality.note: Rubric 0.25: 1970s light fighter without BVR missiles.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: few flying hours on type.

count.note: Air Force: Bell 206 22 + 407 17 + 412 8 + UH-1H 1 + Mi-17 18 + UH-60M 20 + EC725 16 + MD 530F 13 = 115. Navy (Mexican Naval Aviation article, World Air Forces 2024): Mi-17 22 + MD Explorer 6 + UH-60M 9 + EC725 3 + AS565 14 + AS555 1 = 55. Total 170. Trainers excluded. Source for navy part: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Naval_Aviation

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: UH-60M and EC725 modern, many light utility types.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: high operational tempo in counter-narcotics.

count.note: Group 2+ UAVs: Air Force Hermes 450 3. Navy and Army hold some ScanEagle/S4 Ehecatl-class systems; mid/high educated allowance.
Mexican Navy article: Reformador class (Damen SIGMA 10514) frigate Benito Juarez = 1. High allows for a second hull of the 8 planned.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: modern SIGMA frigate with RAM/Harpoon.

count.note: Mexican Navy article: missile boats 2 + OPVs/corvettes 24 (Oaxaca 8, Durango 4, Sierra 3, Holzinger 4, Uribe 5) + coastal patrol 37 (Tenochtitlan 10, Azteca 20, Democrata 2, Cabo 3, Punta 2) + LSTs 2 + Banderas minesweepers 6 = 71. Polaris interceptors (50+) excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: constabulary OPVs, few missiles.

count.note: Educated guess. Army article lists only Bofors L70 40 mm and Oerlikon 35 mm twin guns (quantities not given) and some MANPADS; no SAM batteries. Counted as a handful of gun batteries. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Army)

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5 (competent staff, average generalship): experienced at internal security and disaster relief; no interstate war since 1945 (Escuadron 201) and limited combined-arms exercise culture.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: volunteer force with strong institutional loyalty; desertion and corruption pressure from cartel environment.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5 average; high public trust in the armed forces, but no external threat narrative.

weapons.note: Below anchor 9: no guided anti-tank/anti-air missile mass, towed artillery, F-5 with IR missiles only; modern small arms.

armor.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: no MBTs, light armoured cars and 1970s APCs; MRAP-class vehicles.

ships.note: Near anchor 9: one modern SIGMA frigate with RAM/Harpoon, many OPVs; no submarines.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: no hardened air bases or layered air defence.

logistics.note: Below anchor 9: road/rail transport, small airlift (C-130, C-27J, C-295), domestic industry base.

communications.note: Anchor 9: Mexsat military satellites (Morelos 3), digital radios; limited data links.

isr.note: Anchor 9: E-99 AEW, TPS-78 radars, Mexsat; small UAV fleet.

air.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: 7 F-5E/F, no modern fighter.

cyber.note: Below anchor 10: cyber units within SEDENA/SEMAR, mainly defensive and surveillance (Pegasus use documented).

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 2,891,211,142,079 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 2,314,414,519,234 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/MEX/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 0.74% of GDP in 2025. Low 0.6% (2020), high 0.9% (2024 est., CIA Factbook); internal security spending on the National Guard largely outside this figure.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 30.56% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Large exporter of fruit, vegetables and beef but the largest importer of US maize; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 63,982,817 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 8.844% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 1,131,713. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. SEDENA DGIM builds DN-XI, Cimarron and Holkan light armoured vehicles (1,200 Holkan planned per Infodefensa 2026). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Army)

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. SEMAR shipyards (ASTIMAR) build Tenochtitlan/Damen patrol vessels and OPVs. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Navy)

ships_major.note: Educated guess. SIGMA frigate modules built in Mexico with Damen; slow rate. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Navy)

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 836,603 km total (2020), 175,526 km paved (2021), 11,094 km controlled-access. Mid is paved plus half of the unpaved network (derived midpoint) because much of the unpaved network is rural track; high is the total.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook: 23,389 km standard gauge (2017). Range +/- for concession-network definitions; World Bank has no recent value.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 35 ports, 0 large + 7 medium; key ports Veracruz, Manzanillo, Tampico, Lazaro Cardenas (listed), Ensenada, Mazatlan, Acapulco.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 2,228 thousand DWT under the Mexican flag (1,715 thousand GT), mostly Pemex tankers and offshore vessels. High is an educated allowance for Mexican-owned foreign-flag tonnage.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck-based sustainment of motorized brigades; no expeditionary logistics.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys (roughly 6 million horses plus mules/donkeys; not from FAO data). The Army still has mounted units.

nuclearWarheads.note: Mexico is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Depositary state of the Treaty of Tlatelolco.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: mountainous and desert terrain, large population, strong national identity; no harsh-climate bonus.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:MEX (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2026 as quoted for personnel; Mexican Army, Mexican Air Force, Mexican Navy and Mexican Naval Aviation articles (World Air Forces 2024-2026 tables) for equipment. Many Army equipment rows have no quantity, so ifv_apc and artillery are grade C/D. ships_major = frigates; ships_minor = missile boats, OPVs/corvettes, coastal patrol, LSTs, MCM. National Guard (paramilitary, 136,900 per IISS) excluded; a large share of active forces is committed to internal security, so few are available on day 1 for external war. No tanks: armor role omitted.
